name: Persinger lab: left temporoparietal burst-firing (20 min, comparison arm)
origin: Laurentian University: Richards, Koren & Persinger 1992; Healey, Persinger & Koren 1996; Persinger & Healey 2002
summary: Burst-firing over the left temporoparietal region only, 1 uT for 20 min: the comparison arm of Persinger's lateralisation studies, which by the lab's reports raised neither hypnotic suggestibility (Healey 1996) nor apprehension (Richards 1992) and, with an unnamed 'complex, pulsed' pattern, gave fewer sensed presences than right-sided or bilateral fields (Persinger & Healey 2002).
notes: Healey, Persinger & Koren 1996 gave 20 min of 1-uT burst-firing over the right hemisphere, the left, both or a sham; by the lab's reports the left arm raised neither suggestibility nor, in Richards 1992, apprehension in women, and in Persinger & Healey 2002 it gave fewer presences, fears and odd smells than the right or bilateral arms. Persinger & Healey 2002 (48 people) ran the same four arms at 100 nT-1 uT with fields 'primarily over' one side; they name no pattern ('complex, pulsed'), so burst-firing there is an assumption, and any field they had on the other side is off here. The presence-left program plays the same burst timing on four left-side coils and adds an optional 10 min; this file keeps the 20-min, two-coil form. The lab's burst-firing point values were never published; the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz) stands in, with the file's published length, 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s; Carniello 2020; other theses give 248 or 289), once every 4 s (the lab's rat analgesia work, Martin & Persinger 2004, and Collins 2014's Shiva study; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009 give 'once every 3 s for about 0.7 s'). Two coils, T7 and TP7, are an inference from 'left temporoparietal'; the right channels stay silent. Same coils and pattern as the right and bilateral programs, so it is their active control. Tiller & Persinger 1994 (15 min of a 1-uT 'pulsed' field) reported higher suggestibility only when the right side came first (persinger-tiller-1994-right-then-left), so log the order in any comparison; and a field that raises suggestibility confounds every unblinded session, so compare blind (right, left, persinger-burst-temporal-bilateral, sham). None of these lateral effects has been replicated outside the lab. Independent double-blind tests found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012), and in Granqvist's study suggestibility traits, not the field, predicted the reports. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop at once on fear, headache or distress.
setting: Partial sensory deprivation: blindfold or opaque goggles, reclining in a very quiet, darkened room; the same before-and-after measures as the right arm.
schedule: One 20-min exposure per arm. At most once a week; run right, left, bilateral and sham sessions in blinded, counterbalanced order.
source: Healey, Persinger & Koren 1996, Int J Neurosci 87:201 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9003980/ ; Richards, Koren & Persinger 1992, Percept Mot Skills 75:667 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1408634/ ; Persinger & Healey 2002, J Nerv Ment Dis 190:533 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12193838/ ; Tiller & Persinger 1994, Int J Neurosci 79:157 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7744557/ ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University, p. 89 (230-point burst-firing file, 3-ms points) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Collins 2014, MA thesis 'Investigating the Shiva', Laurentian University, p. 31 (289 points, 3 ms, 4000 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/16d96136-680c-4afe-8044-f9137bd01afc ; Martin & Persinger 2004, Neurosci Lett 366:226 (burst-firing once every 4 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15276252/ ; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009, Electromagn Biol Med 28:374 ('once every 3 s for about 0.7 s') https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20017628/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
